title: Meta ids, token lifetimes, client token pair, placeholders and masked displays
summary: A Page entry in an accounts response without a token, the non-secret members of a token response, a documented request template, a pair of an app id and a client token, and placeholders, references and masked displays under the access_token name.
rationale: A Page id, a user id and a token lifetime are metadata, and a client token is documented as not secret. A placeholder such as the documented request template, a reference or a masked display carries no value. Flagging them would redact identifiers and documentation a reader needs. The case decides nothing about any token kind beyond what it holds.

expectation.rationale: Project policy, maintainer-only (ADR 0020, credential-evidence#235). Finalized by the sole maintainer alone: not reviewed, not independent validation, queued for retro-review (#154). The question, options, strongest dissent and reversing evidence are in the review history. Not flagged under project policy: these inputs hold no access token value. That a client token pair is public and that a placeholder, reference or masked display is not a value are the project's decisions; Meta documents the client token as not secret and the token members (carrier existence only).

sources.supports: Client tokens identify your app when calling app-level APIs from native or desktop apps. Because client tokens are embedded in apps, they are not secret.
